# Stripe Projects

> Stripe Projects is a CLI tool that scaffolds production-ready, full-stack applications with Stripe payments pre-configured. Run one command to get a working app with payments, authentication, a database, and deployment already wired together.

Stripe Projects eliminates the boilerplate that every new application requires. Instead of spending days connecting Stripe, setting up auth, choosing a database, and configuring deployments, developers run a single command and get a fully integrated starting point. Every generated application is immediately ready to accept real payments.

## Getting Started

- [Install command](https://stripe.com/docs): Run `stripe projects create my-app` to scaffold a new application
- [Stripe Documentation](https://stripe.com/docs): Full developer documentation for the Stripe platform
- [GitHub](https://github.com/stripe): Open source code and examples

**Quick start:**
```
stripe projects create my-app
stripe projects init
```

## Features

- **No dashboard hopping** — Eliminate the "dashboard maze" of dozens of sign-ups, configuration steps, and API key hunts. Provision a complete, working stack with one command directly from your CLI.
- **Real infrastructure without lock-in** — We provision real services, not sandboxes. You maintain direct relationships with every provider — accounts in your name, credentials yours to keep.
- **Built for AI-assisted development** — Machine-readable and tool-callable, giving coding agents (like Claude Code or Cursor) the ability to reliably provision and wire up real infrastructure.
- **A central hub for keys and secrets** — One secure, central place to manage credentials and environment variables across your entire stack, automatically injected into your project environment.
- **Seamless upgrades** — Manage paid plan selections and billing across multiple providers without leaving your workflow. One payment method, one place to pay — and your agent can handle it on your behalf.
- **Bring your existing stack** — Link existing third-party service accounts and initialize projects on your current Stripe account, bringing established infrastructure under one control plane.

## Ecosystem — Supported Services

Projects integrates with these services, which can be added via `projects service add <name>`:

- **Stripe** (payments) — Accept one-time payments, subscriptions, and invoices. Pre-wired with no boilerplate. https://stripe.com
- **Clerk** (auth) — Drop-in authentication with social login, magic links, MFA, and full user management UI. https://clerk.dev
- **Supabase** (storage/database) — Open-source Firebase alternative with Postgres, realtime subscriptions, and file storage. https://supabase.com
- **Vercel** (hosting) — Deploy frontend apps to the edge with automatic CI/CD, edge functions, and global CDN. https://vercel.com
- **Neon** (database) — Serverless Postgres with autoscaling to zero, database branching, and a generous free tier. https://neon.tech
- **Railway** (hosting) — Deploy servers, databases, and cron jobs with zero ops overhead. https://railway.app
- **PostHog** (analytics) — Self-hostable product analytics with event capture, session replay, and feature flags. https://posthog.com
- **Sentry** (monitoring) — Full-stack error monitoring, performance tracing, and alerting pre-configured with zero setup. https://sentry.io
- **Chroma** (ai/vector database) — Open-source embedding database for AI applications. https://trychroma.com
- **PlanetScale** (database) — MySQL-compatible serverless database with non-blocking schema changes and branching workflows. https://planetscale.com

## CLI Commands

```
stripe projects create <app-name>     # Scaffold a new application
stripe projects init                  # Initialize services and config
stripe projects service add <name>    # Add an ecosystem service
/contest                              # Submit contest entry from within the CLI
```

## Contest

Run `stripe projects init` and submit `/contest` inside the CLI to enter a giveaway. Winners receive a Mac Mini, openclaw, and Stripe Projects credits. 10 total winners chosen at random. Read more about the rules and terms at https://stripe.com.
